use: an algorithm's first instance slow, then faster
request: Short on insertion sort for my intro CS class. Show the first insert slowly, then let it run.
intent: Students in an intro programming course need to see how insertion sort moves values.
goal: The viewer can describe one insertion and predict how the rest go.
promise: Sorting a hand of cards, one card at a time.
arc: A row of four values, the first insert slowly, the second at normal speed, the rest fast, ending sorted.

events.text: Insertion sort builds a sorted hand, one card at a time, like sorting playing cards.
events.job: Set up the row and the idea of a sorted part on the left.
events.knows: There is a sorted part that grows from the left.
events.waiting: How does a card get into the sorted part?
events.look: the row of four values, with the leftmost marked as the sorted part

events.text: Take the one. The four is bigger, so the one slides in front.
events.knows: A card moves left past every bigger card.
events.look: the 1 and the 4 being compared, then the 1 sliding in front

holds.does: the sorted part, now 1 4, is marked as sorted

phases.why: the first comparison and swap, one step at a time

events.text: Now the three: it passes the four, then stops at the one.
events.job: The second insertion, at normal speed, showing where it stops.
events.knows: A card stops at the first smaller card.
events.look: the 3 moving past the 4 and stopping at the 1

events.text: The two does the same, and the hand is sorted. Every card was compared only with cards already sorted.
events.job: Run the rest fast and land on the sorted row.
events.look: the last insertion running quickly, then the sorted row

phases.why: the rest of the sort runs quickly and comes to rest sorted

measure.derived: Derived once from the request, intent and audience; thresholds not named here take the defaults in bench/lib/settings.ts. Read sizes scale with how wide the frame looks: a classroom or meeting screen from the back looks narrower than a phone at arm's length, a laptop at a desk wider. A hold listed as still is one the plan asks to wait without motion.

context.why: a short for an intro CS class

quiz.q: What was the starting order of the values?
What happened in the first comparison?
quiz.a: The 1 was compared with the 4; the 4 was bigger, so the 1 moved in front of it.

quiz.q: Where did the 3 stop, and why?
quiz.a: Just after the 1 (between 1 and 4), because the 1 is smaller.

quiz.q: Which insertion was shown most slowly?
quiz.a: The first one (the 1 moving in front of the 4).

quiz.q: After the first insertion, what is the order of the whole row?
After the 3 has been inserted, what is the order of the row?
After the second insertion, which number is last in the row?
